question: On 3 January 2026, President Donald Trump, supported by his administration, announced his intention to annex Greenland, justifying it as a matter of ‘national security’. The threat to the Kingdom of Denmark’s autonomous territory – which also wants to become independent – is not new: Donald Trump has been threatening to invade Greenland since his inauguration in 2024.

Those repeated threats to the territorial integrity of a constituent country of an EU Member State violate international law and constitute a direct attack on the sovereignty of the people. They help legitimise the law of the strongest and the violation of international law. The European Union must clearly oppose those threats, in keeping with its fundamental values and with international law.

In the face of American imperialism, the European Union must not yield. In the face of the threat of imminent annexation, the European Union must confirm the end of negotiations on the trade agreement between the European Union and the United States.

Donald Trump must understand that nothing will be negotiated with a power that violates the sovereignty of the people and constantly breaches the rules of international law. How is the Commission planning to: 1.
require that negotiations on the EU-US trade agreement end?
clearly and publicly oppose the United States’ imperialist and colonising desires?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.3.2026) The EU has reacted to the situation concerning Greenland, and the related threat of tariffs on six Member States, with determination and unity. This response proved effective in defending European interests and de-escalating the situation.

The EU expressed unequivocal solidarity with Greenland and the Kingdom of Denmark, it stood firmly with the six Member States threatened with tariffs; and it engaged actively with the US on multiple levels. The EU also signalled that it was well prepared to deploy trade countermeasures and non-tariff instruments if necessary.

In sum, four key principles guided the response – firmness, outreach, preparedness and unity. This approach proved effective. Looking ahead, the Commission will be guided by these same principles. Going forward, the EU should continue cooperating with the US to advance the transatlantic trade relationship on all issues of common interest.
The EU is fully committed to implementing in good faith the EU-US Joint Statement of 21 August 20251.
